title: TYPE 3H FIRE ENGINES
description: The U. S. Forest Service (USFS) is soliciting a proposal from qualified vendors for five (5) Type 3H (Heavy) fire engines, body only configuration, to be installed on Government-furnished 4X4 cab and chassis. Scope includes chassis modifications and preparation, installation of the body, fire pump, 750-gallon water tank, warning lights, required graphics package, and all components necessary to deliver a complete operational unit. Apparatus must meet Forest Service national standard specifications, including compliance with NFPA 1900 unless otherwise specified. Proposal shall include delivery of each unit and on-site familiarization training. Vendors shall demonstrate their capability to produce apparatus meeting the requirements of the USFS, summarized in executive form.

title: Cyber Platform
description: The Government seeks a commercially available Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) cybersecurity training platform that provides immersive, hands-on cyber learning, realistic cyber laboratory environments, structured learning pathways, cyber range exercises, and cybersecurity certification preparation capabilities that enhance cyber workforce readiness, operational problem-solving, critical thinking, and cyber mission effectiveness. The platform shall support Joint Professional Military Education (JPME), Department of Defense (DoD) cyber workforce development initiatives, cyber upskilling, and cyber readiness activities for authorized faculty, staff, and students through Internet-based access to interactive cybersecurity exercises, practical laboratories, and modular cybersecurity training content. See the RFQ for further details

description: *** The purpose of Amendment 0002 is to incorporate the updated Performance Work Statement (PWS) for Solicitation W9124C-26-Q-A024, ATC Turf Field Maintenance, and to provide the Government�s responses to all vendor-submitted questions. *** The objective of this contract is to provide comprehensive maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform turf field grooming, preventive maintenance, minor repair services, and unscheduled/emergency maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall be performed bi-annually to ensure proper turf condition, safety, and performance. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Fort Jackson, South Carolina 29207 BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation method for this requirement. The Government will award one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) C-Type contract to the offeror whose proposal is technically acceptable, has the lowest evaluated price, and is deemed responsible. The Government will evaluate the contractor's Technical Approach, Past Performance, and Price Proposal to ensure that it reflects a sound understanding of this requirement and complies with the requirements in the solicitation. A determination of a fair and reasonable price will be conducted. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Offerors shall submit a signed and dated proposal electronically in accordance with the attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-1 Instructions. Failure to provide all required documents or information may exclude the offeror from further consideration. Proposal Preparation Instructions. The solicitation instructions identify the following proposal volumes: a. Volume 1 � General b. Volume 2 � Technical Approach (to include Capabilities Statement) c. Volume 3 � Past Performance Information d. Volume 4 � Cost/Price EVALUATION: The proposal will be evaluated under three (3) evaluation factors: Factor 1: Technical Factor 2: Past Performance Factor 3: Cost/Price The Technical factor will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. An �Unacceptable� rating in any single Technical element will result in an overall rating of �Unacceptable� for Factor 1. Past Performance will be evaluated as described below. Price will be evaluated for reasonableness. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. Factor 1 � Technical: The Technical factor evaluation provides an assessment of the offeror's capability to satisfy the Government's minimum requirements. The Technical factor has three elements. The Government will evaluate the technical approach, quality controls, and key personnel qualifications related to providing preventive and unscheduled maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson, SC. Element 1: Technical Approach and Understanding The proposal must demonstrate a clear understanding of and a sound approach to performing all services outlined in the PWS, including the specific basic services and tasks described in PWS Part 5. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 1. PWS Compliance: A compliant, clear operational methodology to perform multi-leveling field vacuuming, extensive fiber brush grooming, use of magnetic metal sweepers, and specialized synthetic turf cleaning/sanitization across the fifteen (15) synthetic fields. 2. Operational Responsiveness: A solid approach to executing scheduled semi-annual services and mobilizing personnel/equipment for unscheduled emergency repairs/maintenance in accordance with the response timelines set forth in the PWS. Element 2: Deliverables and Quality Control The proposal must address the deliverables listed in Technical Exhibit B and include the development of a Quality Control Plan (QCP) in accordance with PWS Paragraph 1.5.1. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 3. Reporting & Deliverables Compliance: A compliant administrative framework to compile, track, and electronically deliver all semi-annual reporting, worksheets, and documentation specified in PWS Technical Exhibit B. 4. QCP Framework: A draft Quality Control Plan (QCP) that completely addresses all requirements and criteria outlined in PWS Paragraph 1.5.1, such as lines of authority, deficiency prevention, inspection logging, key controls, and records preservation. Element 3: Key Personnel The proposal must confirm that all Key Personnel meet the minimum qualifications specified in the PWS. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must confirm: 5. PWS Qualifications & Experience: All proposed key personnel meet the minimum standards specified in PWS Paragraph 1.10. This includes confirming that the Contract Manager/Alternate has full authority to act on daily operations, and the Quality Control Manager and Systems Administrator each possess a minimum of five (5) years of direct experience. 6. Special Qualifications: Proof that proposed staff possess and maintain active Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level I professional certifications as required by PWS Paragraph 1.10.d. Technical Factor Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal meets the minimum requirements of the solicitation. UNACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal does not meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Note: An "Unacceptable" rating in any single element will result in an overall rating of "Unacceptable" for Factor 1. Factor 2 � Past Performance: The past performance evaluation will assess the offeror's probability of meeting the solicitation's requirements as indicated by that offeror's record of past performance. Past Performance is assessed at the factor level after evaluating aspects of the offeror's recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant past performance, focusing on services similar to the Turf Field Maintenance requirements. The Government will evaluate past performance based on information submitted per the solicitation instructions and other available sources. Past Performance Evaluation Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort, or the offeror's performance record is unknown. UNACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has no reasonable expectation that the offeror will be able to successfully perform the required effort. NEUTRAL � In the case of an offeror without a record of relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available, the offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, a "Neutral" rating shall be considered "Acceptable." Factor 3 � Cost/Price: The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total proposed price for all performance periods (Base Period plus Option Years 1 through 4). The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the base period and option period prices are significantly unbalanced. As part of price evaluation, the Government will evaluate its option to extend services under RFO FAR Clause 52.217-8 by adding one-half (1/2) of the Offeror's final option year price (Option Year 4) to the Offeror's total evaluated price. title: ATC Turf Field Maintenance
description: The objective of this contract is to provide comprehensive maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform turf field grooming, preventive maintenance, minor repair services, and unscheduled/emergency maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall be performed bi-annually to ensure proper turf condition, safety, and performance. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Fort Jackson, South Carolina 29207 BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation method for this requirement. The Government will award one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) C-Type contract to the offeror whose proposal is technically acceptable, has the lowest evaluated price, and is deemed responsible. The Government will evaluate the contractor's Technical Approach, Past Performance, and Price Proposal to ensure that it reflects a sound understanding of this requirement and complies with the requirements in the solicitation. A determination of a fair and reasonable price will be conducted. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Offerors shall submit a signed and dated proposal electronically in accordance with the attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-1 Instructions. Failure to provide all required documents or information may exclude the offeror from further consideration. Proposal Preparation Instructions. The solicitation instructions identify the following proposal volumes: a. Volume 1 � General b. Volume 2 � Technical Approach (to include Capabilities Statement) c. Volume 3 � Past Performance Information d. Volume 4 � Cost/Price EVALUATION: The proposal will be evaluated under three (3) evaluation factors: Factor 1: Technical Factor 2: Past Performance Factor 3: Cost/Price The Technical factor will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. An �Unacceptable� rating in any single Technical element will result in an overall rating of �Unacceptable� for Factor 1. Past Performance will be evaluated as described below. Price will be evaluated for reasonableness. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. Factor 1 � Technical: The Technical factor evaluation provides an assessment of the offeror's capability to satisfy the Government's minimum requirements. The Technical factor has three elements. The Government will evaluate the technical approach, quality controls, and key personnel qualifications related to providing preventive and unscheduled maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson, SC. Element 1: Technical Approach and Understanding The proposal must demonstrate a clear understanding of and a sound approach to performing all services outlined in the PWS, including the specific basic services and tasks described in PWS Part 5. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 1. PWS Compliance: A compliant, clear operational methodology to perform multi-leveling field vacuuming, extensive fiber brush grooming, use of magnetic metal sweepers, and specialized synthetic turf cleaning/sanitization across the fifteen (15) synthetic fields. 2. Operational Responsiveness: A solid approach to executing scheduled semi-annual services and mobilizing personnel/equipment for unscheduled emergency repairs/maintenance in accordance with the response timelines set forth in the PWS. Element 2: Deliverables and Quality Control The proposal must address the deliverables listed in Technical Exhibit B and include the development of a Quality Control Plan (QCP) in accordance with PWS Paragraph 1.5.1. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 3. Reporting & Deliverables Compliance: A compliant administrative framework to compile, track, and electronically deliver all semi-annual reporting, worksheets, and documentation specified in PWS Technical Exhibit B. 4. QCP Framework: A draft Quality Control Plan (QCP) that completely addresses all requirements and criteria outlined in PWS Paragraph 1.5.1, such as lines of authority, deficiency prevention, inspection logging, key controls, and records preservation. Element 3: Key Personnel The proposal must confirm that all Key Personnel meet the minimum qualifications specified in the PWS. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must confirm: 5. PWS Qualifications & Experience: All proposed key personnel meet the minimum standards specified in PWS Paragraph 1.10. This includes confirming that the Contract Manager/Alternate has full authority to act on daily operations, and the Quality Control Manager and Systems Administrator each possess a minimum of five (5) years of direct experience. 6. Special Qualifications: Proof that proposed staff possess and maintain active Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level I professional certifications as required by PWS Paragraph 1.10.d. Technical Factor Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal meets the minimum requirements of the solicitation. UNACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal does not meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Note: An "Unacceptable" rating in any single element will result in an overall rating of "Unacceptable" for Factor 1. Factor 2 � Past Performance: The past performance evaluation will assess the offeror's probability of meeting the solicitation's requirements as indicated by that offeror's record of past performance. Past Performance is assessed at the factor level after evaluating aspects of the offeror's recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant past performance, focusing on services similar to the Turf Field Maintenance requirements. The Government will evaluate past performance based on information submitted per the solicitation instructions and other available sources. Past Performance Evaluation Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort, or the offeror's performance record is unknown. UNACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has no reasonable expectation that the offeror will be able to successfully perform the required effort. NEUTRAL � In the case of an offeror without a record of relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available, the offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. description: A total of twenty-four (24) sanitation units must be delivered and securely anchored across six (6) designated outdoor training area locations at Fort Eustis, Virginia. All units must be serviced exactly once per week on Wednesdays (between 0700 and 1600 hours). Servicing includes complete tank evacuation, sanitizing and scrubbing, chemical recharging, and fully replenishing all consumables (minimum 2 rolls of toilet paper, hand soap, clean water, and hand sanitizer). title: D--Notice of Intent to Sole Source
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS Prepared in accordance with FAR Part 5 The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), Northwest Regional Office (NWRO), Forestry Program intends to enter into a sole source firm-fixed price contract with the Forest Biometrics Research Institute (FBRI) for an umbrella licensing agreement for specialized software under the authority of FAR 6.103-1 and 41 U.S.C. 1901. The Bureau of Indian Affairs, Northwest Regional Office (NWRO), Forestry Program requires an umbrella licensing agreement for specialized software. This agreement is essential to support the program's capacity to perform comprehensive analyses that inform forest management strategies and harvest planning. The software will provide the necessary framework to ensure that decisions regarding forest stewardship are based on reliable data and best practices, enabling the BIA to fulfill its responsibilities in managing forest resources effectively. FBRI is unique in both structure and service regarding the management of natural resources. The Institute is the only research, service and continuing education organization of this kind throughout the United States and Canada. No other organization, university, USFS Experiment Station or consulting firm provides the scope of services provided by the FBRI. No solicitation is available and no technical questions will be answered for this requirement. The NAICS code for this acquisition is 513210 Software Publishers. If a firm believes that BIA should not pursue this procurement, it should submit a capability statement and pricing information for this requirement by 09:00 am Pacific Time, 14 September 2026. Please contact Brian Roberts, Contracting Officer, via email at brian.roberts@bia.gov.

title: ATC Turf Field Maintenance
description: The objective of this contract is to provide comprehensive maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform turf field grooming, preventive maintenance, minor repair services, and unscheduled/emergency maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall be performed bi-annually to ensure proper turf condition, safety, and performance. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Fort Jackson, South Carolina 29207 BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation method for this requirement. The Government will award one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) C-Type contract to the offeror whose proposal is technically acceptable, has the lowest evaluated price, and is deemed responsible. The Government will evaluate the contractor's Technical Approach, Past Performance, and Price Proposal to ensure that it reflects a sound understanding of this requirement and complies with the requirements in the solicitation. A determination of a fair and reasonable price will be conducted. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Offerors shall submit a signed and dated proposal electronically in accordance with the attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-1 Instructions. Failure to provide all required documents or information may exclude the offeror from further consideration. Proposal Preparation Instructions. The solicitation instructions identify the following proposal volumes: a. Volume 1 � General b. Volume 2 � Technical Approach (to include Capabilities Statement) c. Volume 3 � Past Performance Information d. Volume 4 � Cost/Price EVALUATION: The proposal will be evaluated under three (3) evaluation factors: Factor 1: Technical Factor 2: Past Performance Factor 3: Cost/Price The Technical factor will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. An �Unacceptable� rating in any single Technical element will result in an overall rating of �Unacceptable� for Factor 1. Past Performance will be evaluated as described below. Price will be evaluated for reasonableness. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. Factor 1 � Technical: The Technical factor evaluation provides an assessment of the offeror's capability to satisfy the Government's minimum requirements. The Technical factor has three elements. The Government will evaluate the technical approach, quality controls, and key personnel qualifications related to providing preventive and unscheduled maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson, SC. Element 1: Technical Approach and Understanding The proposal must demonstrate a clear understanding of and a sound approach to performing all services outlined in the PWS, including the specific basic services and tasks described in PWS Part 5. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 1. PWS Compliance: A compliant, clear operational methodology to perform multi-leveling field vacuuming, extensive fiber brush grooming, use of magnetic metal sweepers, and specialized synthetic turf cleaning/sanitization across the fifteen (15) synthetic fields. 2. Operational Responsiveness: A solid approach to executing scheduled semi-annual services and mobilizing personnel/equipment for unscheduled emergency repairs/maintenance in accordance with the response timelines set forth in the PWS. Element 2: Deliverables and Quality Control The proposal must address the deliverables listed in Technical Exhibit B and include the development of a Quality Control Plan (QCP) in accordance with PWS Paragraph 1.5.1. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 3. Reporting & Deliverables Compliance: A compliant administrative framework to compile, track, and electronically deliver all semi-annual reporting, worksheets, and documentation specified in PWS Technical Exhibit B. 4. QCP Framework: A draft Quality Control Plan (QCP) that completely addresses all requirements and criteria outlined in PWS Paragraph 1.5.1, such as lines of authority, deficiency prevention, inspection logging, key controls, and records preservation. Element 3: Key Personnel The proposal must confirm that all Key Personnel meet the minimum qualifications specified in the PWS. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must confirm: 5. PWS Qualifications & Experience: All proposed key personnel meet the minimum standards specified in PWS Paragraph 1.10. This includes confirming that the Contract Manager/Alternate has full authority to act on daily operations, and the Quality Control Manager and Systems Administrator each possess a minimum of five (5) years of direct experience. 6. Special Qualifications: Proof that proposed staff possess and maintain active Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level I professional certifications as required by PWS Paragraph 1.10.d. Technical Factor Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal meets the minimum requirements of the solicitation. UNACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal does not meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Note: An "Unacceptable" rating in any single element will result in an overall rating of "Unacceptable" for Factor 1. Factor 2 � Past Performance: The past performance evaluation will assess the offeror's probability of meeting the solicitation's requirements as indicated by that offeror's record of past performance. Past Performance is assessed at the factor level after evaluating aspects of the offeror's recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant past performance, focusing on services similar to the Turf Field Maintenance requirements. The Government will evaluate past performance based on information submitted per the solicitation instructions and other available sources. Past Performance Evaluation Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort, or the offeror's performance record is unknown. UNACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has no reasonable expectation that the offeror will be able to successfully perform the required effort. NEUTRAL � In the case of an offeror without a record of relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available, the offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, a "Neutral" rating shall be considered "Acceptable." title: 221(d)(4) Afforable Housing Training - HUD
description: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is issuing this source sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for a contractor to provide training services to provide a structured, instructor-led, virtual training program tailored to FHA Section 221(d)(4) multifamily underwriting and affordable housing finance. The training shall strengthen participants' knowledge and practical application of FHA multifamily underwriting principles, including analysis of borrower and project financial information, market and appraisal data, property and capital needs information, environmental considerations, loan documentation, and multifamily lending risks. The Contractor shall be responsible for: Provide training materials that address the required learning areas identified in this SOW. Delivering live virtual instruction to HUD participants. Providing practical examples, exercises, case studies, scenarios, or other applied learning activities relevant to FHA multifamily mortgage transactions. Incorporating participant engagement methods such as discussion questions, knowledge checks, problem-solving activities, financial analysis exercises, or similar instructional techniques. Providing opportunities for participants to analyze and interpret information commonly used in FHA multifamily underwriting. Providing assessments or applied exercises to evaluate participant understanding of key course concepts. Providing documentation identifying participants who successfully complete the training requirements. Coordinating with the Government regarding the training schedule, instructional sequence, participant materials, virtual access, accessibility, and course administration. The Contractor may use commercially available training materials, customized materials, or a combination of both, provided the final training satisfies the requirements of this SOW and is not dependent on a proprietary certification or vendor-specific credential unless separately approved by the Government. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 611430, Professional and Management Development Training. There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; and 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of personnel and risk mitigation. Based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Background: HUD staff involved in FHA multifamily underwriting, technical review, loan processing, and related program activities require a comprehensive understanding of large-scale multifamily lending and the information used to evaluate FHA-insured multifamily mortgage transactions. FHA multifamily transactions require consideration of borrower organizational structures, mortgage credit, financial statements, project income and expenses, physical property conditions, capital needs, environmental factors, market conditions, appraisal and valuation information, loan documentation, and lending risks. HUD staff must be able to analyze and interpret this information, identify material risks, understand how individual underwriting components relate to the overall transaction, and determine how the information affects FHA multifamily underwriting decisions. This training requirement is intended to provide HUD participants with structured and applied instructions that supports the development and enhancement of multifamily underwriting competencies. Training shall be aligned with applicable HUD guidance, including relevant provisions of the current MAP Guide, current approved HUD forms, and other applicable FHA multifamily program requirements. The training shall be aligned with applicable HUD guidance, including relevant provisions of the current Multifamily Accelerated Processing (MAP) Guide, current HUD policies and other applicable FHA multifamily program requirements (https://www.hud.gov/hudclips/letters/mortgagee) General Description of Work: Please see the Statement of Work (SOW) for specifics about the tasks associated with this effort. The Contractor shall provide a virtual instructor-led training program of approximately six to eight weeks in duration during the period of performance. The Government anticipates approximately two live virtual sessions per week, with each session lasting approximately two hours. Offerors may propose an alternative schedule, sequence, or delivery structure, provided the proposed approach satisfies the learning objectives and allows completion within the period of performance. The final training schedule shall be coordinated with and approved by the Government after award. description: The objective of this contract is to provide comprehensive maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform turf field grooming, preventive maintenance, minor repair services, and unscheduled/emergency maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall be performed bi-annually to ensure proper turf condition, safety, and performance. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Fort Jackson, South Carolina 29207 BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation method for this requirement. The Government will award one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) C-Type contract to the offeror whose proposal is technically acceptable, has the lowest evaluated price, and is deemed responsible. The Government will evaluate the contractor's Technical Approach, Past Performance, and Price Proposal to ensure that it reflects a sound understanding of this requirement and complies with the requirements in the solicitation. A determination of a fair and reasonable price will be conducted. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Offerors shall submit a signed and dated proposal electronically in accordance with the attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-1 Instructions. Failure to provide all required documents or information may exclude the offeror from further consideration. Proposal Preparation Instructions. The solicitation instructions identify the following proposal volumes: a. Volume 1 � General b. Volume 2 � Technical Approach (to include Capabilities Statement) c. Volume 3 � Past Performance Information d. Volume 4 � Cost/Price EVALUATION: The proposal will be evaluated under three (3) evaluation factors: Factor 1: Technical Factor 2: Past Performance Factor 3: Cost/Price The Technical factor will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. The Government will evaluate the technical approach, quality controls, and key personnel qualifications related to providing preventive and unscheduled maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson, SC. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 1. PWS Compliance: A compliant, clear operational methodology to perform multi-leveling field vacuuming, extensive fiber brush grooming, use of magnetic metal sweepers, and specialized synthetic turf cleaning/sanitization across the fifteen (15) synthetic fields. 2. Operational Responsiveness: A solid approach to executing scheduled semi-annual services and mobilizing personnel/equipment for unscheduled emergency repairs/maintenance in accordance with the response timelines set forth in the PWS. This includes confirming that the Contract Manager/Alternate has full authority to act on daily operations, and the Quality Control Manager and Systems Administrator each possess a minimum of five (5) years of direct experience. 6. Special Qualifications: Proof that proposed staff possess and maintain active Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level I professional certifications as required by PWS Paragraph 1.10.d. Technical Factor Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal meets the minimum requirements of the solicitation. UNACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal does not meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Note: An "Unacceptable" rating in any single element will result in an overall rating of "Unacceptable" for Factor 1. Factor 2 � Past Performance: The past performance evaluation will assess the offeror's probability of meeting the solicitation's requirements as indicated by that offeror's record of past performance. title: 6630--LAB - VIRAL LOAD MOLECULAR TESTING CPT BRIDGE
description: Special Notice Page 5 of 5 Page 5 of 5 Page 1 of 2 This is a notice of the intent, not a request for quotes. Pursuant to the Revolutionary FAR overhaul (RFO), GSAM 538.7104-3 posting requirements, The Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) on behalf of Veterans Integrated Services Network (VISN) 02 James J. Peters VA Medical Center, intends to award a sole source bridge award to Roche Diagnostics Corporation. Contractor: Roche Diagnostics Corporation Street Address: 9115 Hague Road City, State, Zip: Indianapolis, IN 46256-1025 The Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA), VISN 02, James J. Peters VA Medical Center requires a bridge contract to ensure the continuity of essential viral load molecular diagnostic testing equipment, supplies and services impacting patient care. The aforementioned contractor is currently performing under contract number 36C24226A0010 with the period of performance concluding on September 30, 2026. The anticipated period of performance for the bridge award is six (6) months, from October 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027, with one (1), six (6) month option period. The bridge award will be made under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) GSAM 538.7104-3(b)(ii); only one source is capable of providing the products and services required at the level of quality required because the products and services are highly specialized. As written, the DVAs requirement for molecular testing is able to be fulfilled through GSA s Federal Supply Class (FSC) Group 66 III. FSC Group 66 III, 605-6B was established for the procurement of clinical immunochemistry analyzers and corresponding tests and supplies; this group is a priority strategic source under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), and General Services Acquisition Regulations (GSAR) procedures, and as supplemented by the Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulations (VAAR). A long-term action was competitively awarded under FSC Group 66, from solicitation 36C24226Q0487 on a Cost Per Test (CPT) basis. Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) 36C24226A0041 was awarded to Roche Diagnostics on July 1, 2026. A bridge action is required to ensure continued CPT molecular testing, allowing Roche Diagnostics sufficient time to deliver, install, and validate the new analyzers under BPA 36C24226A0041, subsequently removing the current analyzers after validation (36C24226A0010). Market research obtained prior to the solicitation concluded that no subcontractors were/ are authorized distributors for Roche and/or capable of providing the level of supplies, equipment and services required for this action. Furthermore, no manufacturer exists with the ability to provide equipment, supplies and services for a period of six (6) months due to delivery, installation and validation time frames. Le contractant sera chargé d’appuyer le CCAK et la Délégation de l’UE en Côte d’Ivoire, pour la mise en œuvre et le suivi des stratégies et plans d’actions nationaux dans le cadre du financement de la BEI. Les services en question seront mieux fournis par le prestataire de services pour les raisons suivantes (non exhaustives, éventuellement cumulatives): • Le haut niveau de spécialisation requis n’est pas disponible en interne; • Le besoin de flexibilité et la disponibilité nécessaire pour répondre aux besoins évolutifs et croissants. Le recours à des services de conseil externes est nécessaire pour répondre aux objectifs et aux besoins opérationnels de l’action et notamment i) afin d’accompagner le CCAK dans les défis en termes d’adaptation et de suivi du développement rapide de la filière; II) afin de suivre la mise en œuvre des stratégies et plans d’actions nationaux dans le cadre du financement de la BEI, iii) afin de renforcer les connaissances de l’ensemble des intervenants du secteur pour améliorer la pertinence, l’efficacité et l’inclusivité des politiques et stratégies de mise en œuvre.

title: Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP)
description: This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources; (2) determine whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) the availability of domestically manufactured and commercial services. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should indicate its small business status in its response. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Small businesses are encouraged to respond. For equipment/supply requirements, responses must include the place of manufacturing (i.e. address if supply/equipment is a domestic end product and include country of manufacture). For equipment/supply requirements, small businesses must also address the size status of the manufacturer under the applicable NAICS code (i.e. address Non-Manufacturer Rule). Statement of Need and Purpose: The National Institute on Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) and the NIH Blueprint Neurotherapeutics Network (BPN) [https://www.nih.gov/neuroscience-blueprint], with participation from the Helping to End Addiction Long-term� Pain Therapeutics Development Program (HEAL-PTDP) [https://www.ninds.nih.gov/current-research/trans-agency-activities/ninds-role-heal-initiative/pain-therapeutics-development-program-ptdp], have established a �virtual pharma' network of contract service providers and consultants with extensive industry experience to enable therapeutic (e.g., small molecule, peptide, biologic) development in the NIH research community. This network offers researchers access to a range of industry-style therapeutic development services and expertise, including medicinal chemistry, IND-enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trial infrastructure, with the goal of supporting efforts to advance compounds successfully through Phase 1 clinical testing. The Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP) component has the need to recompete its medicinal chemistry services to support a range of medicinal chemistry activities (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including project management and reporting, compound logistics, shipping, synthesis, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and in vitro absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicology (ADMET) studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its contributors. The ultimate goal of the NIH served by this program and of individual projects is to bring new drugs to market. To this end, the NIH has been granted a Determination of Exceptional Circumstances (DEC) to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) for this contract. The DEC enables the Contributors, Institutes that apply for a Grant, to retain control of the intellectual property for compounds created through the Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP). Program Requirement: The scope of this MCSP program shall be medicinal chemistry services including project management and reporting, compound logistics, synthesis, computational chemistry and in vitro ADMET studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its Contributors. NINDS requires a full service, turn-key medicinal chemistry operation for the development of therapeutics within the mission of NINDS, BPN, HEAL-PTDP and other NIH Institutes. The work may include any individual service or combinations of services including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping. Capable vendors must demonstrate the experience and capability to conduct from 1-10 projects simultaneously in the three chemistry stages: exploratory; hit-to-lead; and lead optimization. Capable vendors must also demonstrate the professional and technical personnel with appropriate experience and work history, appropriate facilities, resources and equipment, as well as the capability to rapidly scale up or down the number of staff dedicated to the MCSP contract, depending on the number of projects underway at any given time. Responses To This Notice Must Address/Provide The Following Information: Small businesses that meet the applicable size standard above and who believe that they possess the requisite capabilities, capacity, and personnel with the experience and qualifications to provide the full range of medicinal chemistry services described above are asked to address each of the areas described in the Program Requirement section below and to submit a response. Please ensure that your response is complete and sufficiently detailed to assist in our evaluation as to whether or not this requirement could be set-aside for small business participation only. (a) Current in-house capability and capacity to perform medicinal chemistry services (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping for 1-10 concurrent projects; (b) Demonstrated experience and success in providing a flexible medicinal chemistry support program optimizing compounds from hits into pre-clinical lead candidates by addressing a broad range of chemical liabilities, including toxicity, low blood-brain barrier penetrability, and metabolic instability by providing routine in vitro pharmacology and toxicology assays and services; (c) Demonstrated capability for productive collaborations with organizations and researchers involved in therapeutic development; (d) Staffing and personnel qualifications, i.e., numbers, availability and type of staff that could be assigned to such a program; their expertise, experience and education, including citation of any formal training; (e) A discussion of the requirements to be performed in-house versus those performed outside the responding organization; and (f) Your organization's name, address and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number; point of contact, including title, telephone number, and email address; and your current small business size status (e.g., small, small disadvantaged business, HUBZone, women-owned, 8(a), veteran-owned, etc. pursuant to the applicable NAICS code 541715. GENERIC MARKETING BROCHURES/CAPABILITY STATEMENTS WILL NOT BE EVALUATED. Please submit one (1) electronic copy of your response via e-mail to Shaun Rostad, at shaun.rostad@nih.gov and one Josh Lazarus, at josh.lazarus@nih.gov in MS Word (doc, docx) or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). The e-mail subject line must specify 75N98026R00144SB. You are encouraged to limit your response to fewer than 20 pages. ALL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 1:00 PM EASTERN STANDARD TIME ON September 14, 2026. title: MIXED-METHODS RESEARCH PROJECT
description: The Public Diplomacy Section of U.S. Embassy Kingston intends to commission a multimodal public sentiment research effort to understand Jamaican adults� attitudes, motivations, knowledge gaps, and information-consumption patterns related to migration, including legal pathways and the risks and consequences associated with irregular migration. Findings will inform a data-driven, metric-oriented public diplomacy messaging strategy targeting priority demographic and geographic audiences in Jamaica. The research will support message development, audience segmentation, channel selection, and future performance measurement. The research shall be designed and implemented in a manner that protects respondent confidentiality, maintains sponsor anonymity during fieldwork where directed by DOS, and produces reliable evidence suitable for strategic communications planning. The successful Offeror shall plan, manage, and complete an integrated mixed-methods research project consisting of: (1) one nationally representative quantitative survey; and (2) one round of eight qualitative focus group discussions conducted across eastern and western Jamaica. The Offeror may perform the work directly or use disclosed and approved subcontractors. The prime Offeror shall remain fully responsible for all subcontractor performance, data protection, quality control, schedule compliance, and deliverables. The Offeror shall identify in its proposal all proposed subcontractors, the portion of work assigned to each, their qualifications, and the controls the prime Offeror will use to manage performance and protect information. Substitutions after award require prior written approval from the Contracting Officer. The primary objectives are to: Generate nationally representative quantitative evidence on migration-related attitudes, motivations, perceived benefits and risks, knowledge of legal pathways, exposure to misinformation, and trusted information sources; Generate qualitative evidence that explains the beliefs, emotions, experiences, social influences, and information environments underlying survey findings; Identify priority audience segments by demographic characteristics, geography, migration intention, media consumption, and other relevant attributes; Identify credible messengers, channels, themes, and message frames that may improve awareness of legal pathways and the risks of irregular migration; Provide actionable recommendations for public diplomacy messaging, content development, audience targeting, and future measurement; and Produce complete, well-documented datasets and methodological records that permit independent review and replication.

title: 59--Intent to Award - Datalogger
description: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) has a requirement for a sole source Purchase Order with Campbell Scientific for datalogger systems. The period of performance of the resulting award will be 60 days after award. USGS-Department of State Landslide Disaster Assistance Team (LDAT) plans to purchase data loggers and accessories required to maintain data collection at landslide monitoring sites. To ensure continuity of operations and establish new landslide monitoring sites, LDAT is purchasing common accessories and replacement parts that are most likely needed to ensure that parts are readily available for prompt donation and installation on an as needed basis. Therefore, it intends to make a direct award to Campbell Scientific on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). This is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals but rather an intent to award sole source notification. Questions or concerns may be addressed to the Contract Specialist, Jonathan Wyatt at jonathan_wyatt@ios.doi.gov no later than 09/18/2026. Please see attachment 1 for Sole Source information. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) considers employee signatures to be Personal Protected Information, and therefore all employee signatures have been redacted. By posting this document, the Contracting Officer attests all appropriate signatures have been obtained.

title: NIH NIAID Genedata Analyst bioinformatics software program
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a separate request for quote. The Government�s solicitation for this requirement is provided through the associated combined synopsis/solicitation. The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), Laboratory of Infectious Diseases (LID), Viral Pathogenesis and Evolution Section (VPES), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to Genedata (USA), Inc. for the renewal of Genedata Analyst software. The purpose of this requirement is to provide continued access to Genedata Analyst, a bioinformatics analysis program currently used by VPES to perform comprehensive statistical modeling of multi-omics data and advanced visualizations for target-of-interest identification, biological network characterization, and diagnostic and prognostic biomarker identification in genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics data sets from animal model and human clinical samples derived from vaccine and infection studies. Genedata Analyst provides integrated data normalization, statistical analysis, machine learning, interactive data analysis, visualization, and proprietary data-mapping capabilities. The software supports analytical methods including linear and nonlinear normalization, parametric and non-parametric statistical testing, principal components analysis, mixed linear models, multiple-testing corrections, trend and time-series analysis, decision trees, partial least squares analysis, linear discriminant analysis, feature selection, and model validation. The software also provides interactive data visualization capabilities, including histograms, bar charts, box plots, heat maps, scatter plots, trees, maps, and parallel-coordinate plots. Genedata Analyst includes specialized viewers for interpretation of complex statistical analyses, with interactive features that support data exploration across multiple analytical views. Genedata Analyst supports VPES research directed toward understanding the molecular basis and pathogenesis of respiratory viral disease and the development and evaluation of novel vaccines, antiviral drugs, and therapies. VPES uses genomic, proteomic, computational modeling, and machine-learning approaches to analyze human and animal model data generated through vaccine and infection studies. The requirement is for the renewal of Genedata Analyst software for a 12-month period of performance beginning upon award. Justification for Single Source Genedata (USA), Inc. is the proposed single source for the continued use of Genedata Analyst. This is a follow-on requirement necessary to maintain continuity of VPES�s established bioinformatics analysis environment and ongoing research activities. Genedata Analyst combines data normalization, statistical analysis, machine learning, interactive data visualization, and proprietary data-mapping capabilities within the existing VPES research environment. These integrated capabilities are used to analyze complex multi-omics data generated from clinical and experimental vaccine and infection studies. VPES has more than 100 million gene-expression data points generated from more than eight years of clinical and experimental vaccine-development studies. These historical data and the analytical workflows developed within the Genedata Analyst environment are critical to ongoing long-term clinical immunology, universal vaccine testing, and infectious-disease research. Continued use of Genedata Analyst supports consistency of analytical methods, continuity of established workflows, and continued use of historical research data. Replacing the existing software environment would require evaluation and migration of historical data, redevelopment and validation of established analytical workflows, implementation of replacement software capabilities, and retraining of users. These transition activities could result in duplicative costs, disruption to ongoing research, and delays to VPES scientific activities. The Government requires continued access to the established Genedata Analyst capabilities to maintain continuity of ongoing research activities. Authority This acquisition is being conducted under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) FAR Part 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR Part 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. For purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, contracting officers may solicit from a single source when the Contracting Officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. Submission of Capability Statements Interested parties capable of providing the same or similar products or services must submit a capability statement electronically. Responses will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements must demonstrate the ability to provide Genedata Analyst software or an equivalent solution capable of meeting the Government�s requirements while maintaining compatibility and continuity with VPES�s existing research data, established analytical workflows, and ongoing clinical and experimental vaccine and infection studies. Capability statements must also demonstrate the ability to provide equivalent functionality for multi-omics data analysis, data normalization, statistical analysis, machine learning, interactive data visualization, data mapping, and analysis of genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics data without disruption to ongoing VPES research activities. title: Airfield Electrical and Pavement Rehabilitation Upgrades_Moses Lake Auxiliary Field
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Seattle District (NWS), Special Projects Branch at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), WA has issued this Sources Sought notice for market research purposes. The responses to this notice will be used to develop the Acquisition Strategy for an upcoming Request For Proposal (RFP) to perform airfield electrical and pavement rehabilitation upgrades at the Moses Lake Auxiliary Field. This is not a pre-solicitation announcement, nor an RFP. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this Sources Sought and no contract shall be awarded from this Sources Sought. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information requests. After review of the responses to this notice, and if the Government still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a separate synopsis may be published in the US Government System for Award Management (SAM) Contract Opportunities website at https://www.sam.gov. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to determine the availability, interest, and technical capability of qualified business concerns who demonstrated capabilities in meeting the project description listed below and to receive critical feedback from industry experts regarding the feasibility of the proposed schedule, staffing, and technical requirements. The proposed work is to be performed under the following North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code: 237310 � Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction. Both large and small business firms are encouraged to respond to this Sources Sought notice. However, if sufficient numbers of small business firms demonstrate interest, capabilities, and qualifications, the Government may choose to set-aside the acquisition for small businesses. For the purposes of this procurement, a firm is a small business if its annual average gross revenue, taken the last 3 fiscal years, does not exceed $45,000,000.00. For more information concerning NAICS and a SBA size standards, go to http://www.sba.gov. The following information is tentative and meant to provide interested firms with an idea of the general nature of the anticipated work. The Government reserves the right to update this information as project planning documentation is updated. The information below represents the most current information available and may be superseded upon publication of the preliminary planning information, which may be provided by the Government in the subsequent synopsis. Overview of Anticipated Contract: The Seattle District Corps of Engineers, under FAR Part 36 procurement procedures, anticipates issuing a Request For Proposal (RFP) and subsequent award for Construction Services to perform airfield electrical and pavement rehabilitation upgrades at the Moses Lake Auxiliary Field. The magnitude of construction for this project is estimated to be more than $10,000,000. Background & Scope of Work: The project involves the Maintenance and Rehabilitation (M&R) of airfield pavements and critical electrical systems on Runway 09/27 and Taxiway Foxtrot at the Moses Lake Auxiliary Field, located at Grant County International Airport (GCIA) in Moses Lake, WA. This airfield serves active U.S. Air Force tenant operations. Core Project Components: Pavement Rehabilitation: Demolition, grading, re-paving of Asphaltic Concrete (AC) and Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavements, crack repairs, joint sealing, and spall/patching repairs. Airfield Lighting Upgrades: Installation of new in-pavement light fixtures, augering light base locations, setting cans, pouring rapid-set concrete collars, laying new distribution paths, and pulling new #8 5kV conductors. Vault Equipment Upgrades: Complete overhaul of the remote military operations runway vault equipment, including rigging and mounting new Constant Current Regulators (CCRs), installing airfield lighting control and monitoring system (ALCMS) panels, and integrating Pilot Controlled Lighting (PCL) systems. SCHEDULE & CRITICAL PHASING CONSTRAINTS A key challenge of this procurement is the execution schedule. The Statement of Work (SOW) dictates strict operational constraints to minimize disruption to both military operations and GCIA�s active commercial runways: Airfield Closure Limit: The total airfield closure window is restricted to a maximum of 60 calendar days between April 1st and September 30th in a single construction season. Final cleanup and site turnover must be completed within this 60-day window. Phase 1 (West Taxiway F) Restriction: Must be completed within a 14-to-21-day maximum to minimize temporary closures of the adjacent active commercial Runway 04/22. Phase 2 (East Taxiway F) Restriction: Must be completed within a 14-to-21-day maximum to minimize temporary closures of the adjacent active commercial Runway 14L/32R. Standard Working Hours: Restricted to Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. However, 24/7 operations and overtime are authorized upon pre-approval and joint planning with GCIA and the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). Proposed 58-Day Electrical Milestones: The Government has developed a tentative 58-day electrical schedule within the 60-day closure window: Phase 1: Demo & Make-Safe (6 Days) � Isolate circuits, remove runway/taxiway fixtures, and demolish legacy vault equipment (ACE2, ALCMS). Phase 2: Trenching & Ductbanks (9 Days) � Trench RWY 9-27 distribution paths, lay conduit, and pour localized concrete encasements. Phase 3: Vault Equipment Install (10 Days, concurrent with Phase 2) � Rig/mount new CCRs, install ALCMS panels, prep terminal blocks. Phase 4: Pull Cans & Cabling (10 Days) � Set new pull cans with concrete collars; pull new #8 5kV conductors. Phase 5: In-Pavement Fixtures (8 Days) � Auger light base locations, set cans, and pour rapid-set concrete collars via on-site batch plant. Phase 6: Joint Sealing & Testing (5 Days) � Sawcut/seal concrete joints around light cans and perform Megger testing on all loops. Phase 7: System Commissioning (4 Days) � ALCMS integration, operational burn-in testing, and final turnover punch walks. STANDARD GOVERNMENT CREW ESTIMATES The Government's schedule assumes the deployment of three specialized, dedicated crews:. Crew A: Airfield Electrical (6 Personnel) � 1 Foreperson, 2 Journeymen, 2 Labors, 1 Equipment Operator. (Focus: Field demo, conduit laying, cable pulling, setting light bases). Crew B: Vault & Controls (3 Personnel) � 1 Lead Controls Electrician, 1 Labor, 1 Testing Tech. (Focus: Vault regulators, ALCMS, and systems commissioning). Crew C: Targeted Concrete/Civil (4 Personnel) � 1 Batch Plant Operator, 1 Equipment Operator, 2 Concrete Placers/Finishers. title: Speed Trailers
description: The Government has a requirement for the procurement of two (2) 18-inch speed display radar trailers and two (2) 50-watt solar panels to keep them powered. Vendors are requested to provide a firm-fixed-price quote. The units must meet these salient characteristics: Radar and Display Characteristics: 18-Inch LED Digit Display: Ultra-bright, high-intensity amber (or multi-color red/yellow) LED characters that are highly visible from distances up to 1,000 feet. Radar System: Must be able to measure both approaching and departing directions (dual direction) with the ability to turn off or select one of those directions. 2. Power & Solar Configuration 50-Watt Solar Panel: Highly efficient monocrystalline solar panel mounted on a bracket to provide continuous trickle-charging to the battery bank. Battery Power Bank: Equipped with one (minimum) deep-cycle marine/AGM batteries (Group 24 or equivalent, around 80�100 Ah total capacity) to provide up to 7 to 14 days of autonomous operation without sunlight. Smart Charger: An onboard smart battery charger with an AC shore power outlet to recharge batteries manually when needed. 3. Construction & Physical Security Trailer Chassis: Built from rugged, heavy-duty welded steel tubing (typically 2-inch square 11-gauge steel) with a powder-coated, rust-resistant. Stabilization: Equipped with 3 or 4 retractable, adjustable jacks/stabilizers to lift the tires and secure the trailer in place, even in high winds. Vandalism Protection: Secure, lockable steel enclosure housing the batteries and controllers to prevent unauthorized access or tampering. Display Window: A durable, shatter-resistant, and UV-stabilized Lexan� or polycarbonate window protecting the LED face from road debris and vandalism. 4. Controller & Software Capabilities Local Controls: Push-button, rotary dial, or touchscreen local interfaces located in a locked enclosure. Automatic Brightness: Integrated ambient light sensor that automatically dims the LEDs at night to conserve battery power and brightens them during direct sunlight for visibility. Timers: Need auto shut off after an hour of usage in the event the unit is left on to prevent unnecessary battery drain, not necessarily a timing system with schedules.

title: Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP)
description: This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources; (2) determine whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) the availability of domestically manufactured and commercial services. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should indicate its small business status in its response. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Small businesses are encouraged to respond. For equipment/supply requirements, responses must include the place of manufacturing (i.e. address if supply/equipment is a domestic end product and include country of manufacture). For equipment/supply requirements, small businesses must also address the size status of the manufacturer under the applicable NAICS code (i.e. address Non-Manufacturer Rule). Statement of Need and Purpose: The National Institute on Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) and the NIH Blueprint Neurotherapeutics Network (BPN) [https://www.nih.gov/neuroscience-blueprint], with participation from the Helping to End Addiction Long-term� Pain Therapeutics Development Program (HEAL-PTDP) [https://www.ninds.nih.gov/current-research/trans-agency-activities/ninds-role-heal-initiative/pain-therapeutics-development-program-ptdp], have established a �virtual pharma' network of contract service providers and consultants with extensive industry experience to enable therapeutic (e.g., small molecule, peptide, biologic) development in the NIH research community. This network offers researchers access to a range of industry-style therapeutic development services and expertise, including medicinal chemistry, IND-enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trial infrastructure, with the goal of supporting efforts to advance compounds successfully through Phase 1 clinical testing. The Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP) component has the need to recompete its medicinal chemistry services to support a range of medicinal chemistry activities (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including project management and reporting, compound logistics, shipping, synthesis, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and in vitro absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicology (ADMET) studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its contributors. The ultimate goal of the NIH served by this program and of individual projects is to bring new drugs to market. To this end, the NIH has been granted a Determination of Exceptional Circumstances (DEC) to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) for this contract. The DEC enables the Contributors, Institutes that apply for a Grant, to retain control of the intellectual property for compounds created through the Medicinal Chemistry Support Program for Therapeutic Development (MCSP). Program Requirement: The scope of this MCSP program shall be medicinal chemistry services including project management and reporting, compound logistics, synthesis, computational chemistry and in vitro ADMET studies in support of preclinical drug discovery efforts supported by NIH, NINDS and its Contributors. NINDS requires a full service, turn-key medicinal chemistry operation for the development of therapeutics within the mission of NINDS, BPN, HEAL-PTDP and other NIH Institutes. The work may include any individual service or combinations of services including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping. Capable vendors must demonstrate the experience and capability to conduct from 1-10 projects simultaneously in the three chemistry stages: exploratory; hit-to-lead; and lead optimization. Capable vendors must also demonstrate the professional and technical personnel with appropriate experience and work history, appropriate facilities, resources and equipment, as well as the capability to rapidly scale up or down the number of staff dedicated to the MCSP contract, depending on the number of projects underway at any given time. Responses To This Notice Must Address/Provide The Following Information: Businesses who believe that they possess the requisite capabilities, capacity, and personnel with the experience and qualifications to provide the full range of medicinal chemistry services described above are asked to address each of the areas described in the Program Requirement section below and to submit a response. Please ensure that your response is complete and sufficiently detailed to assist in our evaluation as to whether or not this requirement could be set-aside for small business participation only. (a) Current in-house capability and capacity to perform medicinal chemistry services (exploratory, hit-to-lead and lead optimization phases) including SAR analysis and design, synthesis, in vitro ADMET, computational chemistry/Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) and compound logistics of storage and shipping for 1-10 concurrent projects; (b) Demonstrated experience and success in providing a flexible medicinal chemistry support program optimizing compounds from hits into pre-clinical lead candidates by addressing a broad range of chemical liabilities, including toxicity, low blood-brain barrier penetrability, and metabolic instability by providing routine in vitro pharmacology and toxicology assays and services; (c) Demonstrated capability for productive collaborations with organizations and researchers involved in therapeutic development; (d) Staffing and personnel qualifications, i.e., numbers, availability and type of staff that could be assigned to such a program; their expertise, experience and education, including citation of any formal training; (e) A discussion of the requirements to be performed in-house versus those performed outside the responding organization; and (f) Your organization's name, address and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number; point of contact, including title, telephone number, and email address; and your current small business size status (e.g., small, small disadvantaged business, HUBZone, women-owned, 8(a), veteran-owned, etc. pursuant to the applicable NAICS code 541715. GENERIC MARKETING BROCHURES/CAPABILITY STATEMENTS WILL NOT BE EVALUATED. Please submit one (1) electronic copy of your response via e-mail to Shaun Rostad, at shaun.rostad@nih.gov and one Josh Lazarus, at josh.lazarus@nih.gov in MS Word (doc, docx) or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). The e-mail subject line must specify 75N98026R00144SB. You are encouraged to limit your response to fewer than 20 pages. ALL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 1:00 PM EASTERN STANDARD TIME ON September 14, 2026. The National Institutes of Health, Office of the Director on behalf of the National Institute of Aging (NIA) intends to negotiate and award a purchase order for brand name or equal Multiplexed precision proteomics immunoassay panel for neurological disease biomarkers and bulk reagents that are compatible with the ARGO HT System. The identification of clinically relevant biomarkers for neurological disorders is critical in the development of better tools for diagnosis, disease progression, and prediction of therapeutic outcomes. NIA requires a brand name or equal NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel to provide comprehensive coverage of the hallmarks of neurodegenerative disease with highly sensitive and specific multiplexed analysis of 220 biomarkers using only 25 ?L of sample, providing researchers with an automated solution to dissect disease heterogeneity, uncover co-pathologies, and identify signatures of disease prognosis, progression, and therapeutic response in clinical cohorts. title: Z--Canals Clearing, Sabine NWR, Hackberry, LA
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is issuing a Request for Quotes for the Canals Clearing at the Sabine NWR, Hackberry, LA. The anticipated performance period is shown below. Period of Performance: September 15, 2026 � September 15, 2027 Solicitation 140FS326R0011 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) is 100% Small Business Set Aside and is conducted under FAR Parts 12 and 13, incorporating provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC Number: 2026-01, Effective Date: 03/13/2026. The applicable North American Classification System (NAICS) code is 115310, Support Activities for Forestry. The small business size standard is $34 Million. Terms & Conditions: Any additional contract requirement(s) or terms and conditions determined by the contracting officer to be necessary for this acquisition and consistent with customary commercial practices are attached included in the Attachment Solicitation-provisions and clauses- 140FS326R0011. The full text of the referenced FAR clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/far/ or see terms & conditions attached to the solicitation. In order to be eligible for award, all contractors must have an Active Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) website https://sam.gov/content/home. Please note, SAM is a free website and there is never a cost to register your entity. Prior to or following receipt of an award, the Contractor must register with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Invoice Processing Platform System (IPP) to submit requests for payment. Please note, IPP is a free website and there is never a cost to complete registration. Invoices for services will be paid after the end of the month of service, advanced payments are not allowed. Instructions For all Instructions to Offerors please reference Attachments 1-4. Important Submission Dates & Site Visit Info: 1. Site Inspection: Prior to submitting a quote, offerors or quoters are urged and expected to inspect the site where services are to be performed and to satisfy themselves regarding all general and local conditions that may affect the cost of contract performance. The Site POC is currently on a fire assignment, so vendors interested in viewing the site can have access to the project area with a surface drive boat but if you bring an airboat, you will need permission from the refuge manager prior to access. Boating rules are posted on the Sabine NWR website. Site visits can be scheduled after September 3rd with the Refuge POC Sami Gray at sami_gray@fws.gov, 228-217-3256. 2. Question Submission: All questions regarding this Solicitation must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist, Fred Riley at Fred_riley@ios.doi.gov no later than Thursday, September 10, 2026, at 2:00pm EDT. If necessary, questions received will be answered through an Amendment to this Solicitation. Emails must indicate the following in the subject line: Question Submission for 140FS326R0011. 3. Quote Submission: Quotes (including all required documents) must be transmitted via e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Fred Riley at fred_riley@ios.doi.gov, no later than Monday, September 14, 2026, at 2:00pm EDT. Emails must indicate the following in the subject line: Quote Submission 140FS326R0011. Required Submittal Documents: Offerors responding to this solicitation must submit the following documents: - See Attachment 1- Solicitation- provisions_and_clauses-_FS326R0011- ADDENDUM TO 52.212-1, INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS Complete the attached document or your own version that addresses each element. Your quote will be considered non-responsive and will not be considered if all the above required documents are not completed in full and received as part of your submittal package. An award will be made to the Contractor whose submittal documents conform to the requirements as described in this solicitation and who, based on a subjective assessment from the Government, offers the best value to include technical, past experience, and price. The Government reserves the right to award a contract to other than the lowest priced offer if, in its judgment, the non-cost factors outweighs the price difference. CONTRACT DOCUMENTS, EXHIBITS, OR ATTACHMENTS See attached documents: ATTACHMENT 1 Performance Work Statement ATTACHMENT 2 Quote Schedule ATTACHMENT 3 SCA Wage Determination ATTACHMENT 4 Past Performance Questionnaire Contracting Officer/Office: Fred Riley, Contract Specialist U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Hadley, MA Joint Administrative Operations (JAO) fred_riley@ios.doi.gov
